newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean shares continue weaker on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean shares continue weaker on Wednesday.

text.p: Zimbabwe's key industrial index slipped 8.59 points to close at 10,293.96 on Wednesday and brokers said most investors were still waiting on the sidelines for the government's annual budget announcement before making any moves.

"The big news that investors are waiting for is the government budget in July," one broker said, adding that the government needed to show concrete evidence of it's intention to keep inflation down and to cut down on the budget deficit by reducing its spending, currently swallowing up 40 percent of gross domestic product.

Annual inflation fell to 20.7 percent in the year to May from 22.4 percent in April, but market analysts say it is likely to go up again in June when recent price increases, including fuel, are filtered in. Resultant high interest rates should continue luring investors to the local money market, they say.

Counters to weaken on Wednesday included financial house udc which shed 15 cents to 260, Gulliver which was down 10 cents at 290 and Zimbabwe Newspapers and Randalls which both lost five cents to 115.

In minings, coal miners Wankie and gold producers Rio Tinto RTNR both traded at previous levels but a 10 cent gain in Falgold and a 500 cent jump to 11,500 in gold giant Ashanti nudged the seven-share index 8.79 points to 958.29.
